result: MS023 treatment increases MuSC proliferation and prevents precocious differentiation. MS023-treated MuSCs showed increased Pax7+/ki67+ cells, larger clusters, expanded Pax7+/MyoD+ activated cells, reduced Pax7-/MyoD+ committed cells, increased Pax7+/MyoD- stem-like cells, and enhanced long-term culture capacity up to passage 14.
evaluation: Multiple reviewers explicitly affirm these findings. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'show that small molecule inhibition of Type I PRMTs in muscle stem cells (MSCs) can result in the expansion of this cell type in vitro' and notes this 'advance will likely facilitate CRISPR-based screening approaches.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'they demonstrate that the type I PRMT inhibitor MS023 enhances self-renewal and in vitro expansion of muscle stem cells.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'an enhanced proliferative capacity of cultured MuSCs with an increase of Pax7+/MyoD- cells' and notes these observations are 'more or less in line with previous studies.'

result: The MS023 proliferation effect is mediated by PRMT1 inhibition rather than CARM1. Treatment with the CARM1-specific inhibitor TP-064 did not increase MuSC cell number, and PRMT1 is the most highly expressed type I PRMT in MuSCs at all time points tested.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 acknowledges the authors 'exclude a role for CARM1 in the expansion of MSC cell numbers by treatment with a very specific CARM1 inhibitor, TP064,' indicating PRMT1 is 'likely the main driver.' However, Reviewer 3 raises significant concerns: 'Control experiments with the TP-064 inhibitor...were not done for the transplantation and muscle strength experiments, which is a clear shortcoming.' They note MS023 has 'comparable IC50 values for PRMT1 and PRMT4 (CARM1)' and argue that 'gene expression of Prmt1 is highest among the type I PRMTs in MuSCs...is a rather poor argument, as seen by the strong effects caused by the inactivation of PRMT4.'

result: Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed MS023-treated MuSCs segregate into distinct subpopulations (M3 and M5) with elevated Pax7 expression and markers of quiescence. UMAP analysis identified 10 distinct clusters, with MS023-treated cells showing unique distribution patterns and higher Pax7 expression comparable to quiescent day 0 MuSCs.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 describes the scRNA-seq approach as 'very rigorous' and confirms the authors 'demonstrate that distinct sub-populations of cells emerge under type I PRMT inhibition.' However, Reviewer 3 expresses concern about 'the separation of the subclusters, which appear more or less in the same cloud,' noting 'the transcriptional differences are minor, otherwise one would have seen a much better separation of the subpopulations.' This suggests uncertainty about the biological significance of the identified clusters despite the technical rigor.

result: MS023-treated MuSCs exhibit metabolic reprogramming with upregulated glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation. ScRNA-seq showed enrichment for respiratory electron transport and ATP synthesis pathways, validated by Seahorse assays showing increased OCR, ECAR, glucose uptake, lactate production, and MitoTracker staining.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 acknowledges the authors 'revealed a shift in metabolism in these cells, which they confirmed in vitro.' However, Reviewer 3 raises significant concerns: 'The authors have not done additional experiments but simply toned-down the statements about the relevance of the proposed "metabolic reprogramming"...which was a major conclusion in the original submission.' They note 'the changes in the expression of metabolically relevant genes upon MS023 treatment are interesting and should be analyzed in respect to causality. It is not a solution to more or less disabandon the original hypothesis by changing the wording.'

result: MS023 treatment reversibly blocks differentiation. Cells differentiated in the presence of MS023 showed impaired myotube formation (19% fusion index vs 77% for DMSO), but upon MS023 removal, differentiation capacity was fully restored (76% fusion index comparable to 78% for control).
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly affirms this finding, stating 'Importantly, once the inhibitor is removed these stem cells differentiate "normally"' and notes this addresses the key question of 'whether PRMT1 small molecule inhibition of MSCs will also facilitate the expansion of these cells, and if the removal of the inhibitor after expansion will result in a large functional pool of MSCs.' No reviewer challenges this reversibility finding.

result: MS023-treated MuSCs show enhanced engraftment capacity. Transplanted MS023-treated MuSCs produced more GFP+ mature muscle fibers (88 vs 31 fibers/section, p=0.02) and yielded ~7-fold increase in GFP+ cells following muscle regeneration (p=0.004).
evaluation: Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'Mice receiving the MS023-treated MSCs produced more than double the mature GFP+ muscle fibers than cells treated with DMSO.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'they demonstrate that MS023 enhances muscle stem cell engraftment in vivo.' However, Reviewer 3 raises critical concerns: 'I specifically asked the authors to check whether the dramatic six-fold increase of MuSC engraftment after MS023 treatment really goes along with the incorporation of transplanted MuSC into the MuSC niche, raising concerns that a huge share of the transplanted cells may linger around in the interstitium. It should be very easy to identify and quantify transplanted MuSC outside and inside the basal lamina. Instead of doing the requested experiment, the authors argue about suppression of endogenous MuSC competition by irradiation.'

result: MS023 treatment improves muscle function in mdx mice. Three-day MS023 treatment increased 2-paw grip strength by 50% (p=0.0113), 4-paw grip strength by 45% (p=0.0089), force production by ~30% (p=0.00727), and reduced fiber size variation (p=0.04), with effects persisting 30 days post-treatment.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'A mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy displayed grip strength improvement after just one treatment of MS023,' calling the findings 'stunning' and demonstrating 'therapeutic value.' Reviewer 2 states 'they demonstrate that the direct injection of MS023 increases muscle strength in a mice model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.' However, Reviewer 3 expresses strong skepticism: 'I expressed my doubts that a 3-day treatment with MS023 is sufficient to dramatically enhance muscle function in mdx mice via "improvement" of the MuSC population...even 30 days after administration of MS023. It seems much more likely that MS023 exerts additional effects that are responsible for the dramatic improvement of muscle function in mdx mice...It has to be made clear whether this is really due to "improved" functions of MuSC. Many other processes might be involved or responsible for the effect (e.g. impact on inflammation?).'

result: Trajectory analysis of scRNA-seq data revealed MS023-treated cells emerge later in pseudotime and closer to the differentiation branchpoint. The analysis identified three cell states (quiescence, myoblast, differentiating myoblast) with high replicate correlation (>0.98) and distinct gene expression patterns along trajectory branches.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 describes the scRNA-seq approach as 'very rigorous,' implicitly supporting the trajectory analysis methodology and findings. No reviewer challenges the trajectory analysis results or the technical quality of the scRNA-seq data. The high Pearson correlation and clear separation of cell states along pseudotime are accepted without critique.
